title: Choose the visual world for DevManager
question: The roll assigned the jeepney route placard. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Every option ships with a light/dark toggle.

options.label: Route Placard
options.thesis: Setup is a route: every step is a stop painted on the placard, and you always know where you're riding to.
options.viewport: Standard left step rail and work panel; across the top, a painted route plate lists every setup stop with the current one lit in signal red.
options.risk: Assumes the audience reads jeepney culture as home (not confirmed) and can tip into kitsch if the plate is over-decorated.

raised.raise: Every version, size, port and MB figure sits in strict tabular columns.
Download sizes are drawn as bars whose length is the exact MB.
Every component carries the same fixed fact set: version, size, support end.
A disk budget shows selected downloads against free space and refuses to overflow.
Hairline module borders and tight spacing instead of padded cards.

options.label: Line Map
options.thesis: Your stack is a transit network: each service is a coloured line, each setup step a station.
options.viewport: The step rail is drawn as a line with stations; the work panel lists components, each with its own line colour.
options.risk: Transit-map status displays are a familiar device in dev tools; distinctive only if the line system stays strict.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: One yellow band always shows the next decision, nothing else competes with it.
options.viewport: A yellow band across the panel top names the current decision with a monumental step number; standard rail and controls below.
options.case: Clearest for a step-by-step setup; loses on audience identification, nobody's home world.
options.risk: A full yellow band in dark mode is hard to balance; can feel like a warning.

options.label: High-Density Modules
options.thesis: Pack every fact into ruled modules.
options.viewport: A mosaic of ruled modules per component.
options.case: Loses both axes: too dense for students, and a wizard needs focus.
options.kept: Strict hairline module borders instead of padded cards.

options.label: Data Field
options.thesis: Numbers as a strobing barcode field.
options.viewport: A barcode lattice behind the setup.
options.case: Loses both axes: strobing is hostile to a setup task.

options.label: Dance Score
options.viewport: A vertical score of install steps.
options.case: Loses both axes: no one in this audience reads a dance score.
options.kept: Length encodes an exact quantity (download MB).

options.label: Character Roster
options.thesis: Each component as a mascot with a name plate.
options.case: Loses both axes: trivialises system changes.
options.kept: Every item carries the same fixed fact set.

options.label: Mixtape J-Card
options.thesis: Side A / side B timed to fit the tape.
options.case: Loses both axes: handwriting undercuts precise setup data.
options.kept: A capacity budget that must not overflow (downloads vs free disk).
options.risk: Reads as nostalgia, not a tool.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What dev-environment managers ship, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Sidebar steps, white work panel, blue primary button: the arrangement every user expects.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
